task: 08.04 Breed Knowledge Base and linked prompts
scope: Public breed standards and lexical taxonomy tied to the local draft. The review provides evidence for the project approver. Access was limited to the local KB, prompt and mapping metadata, and public sources. The repository was inspected read-only.
source_locator_convention: PDF page numbers are one-based. Line numbers are extracted-text coordinates used for this review and may change with rendering.

aliases.contract: NFC, casefold, NFC, and collapsed whitespace. Resolve the longest complete phrase. A standalone shared alias gives ambiguous with sorted candidates. Canonical IDs and exact names stay bound to the mapping.
review_notes: Stanford WordNet labels Eskimo dog and husky together in the taxonomy example. The shared alias husky also occurs in the Siberian Husky class. Retain the ambiguous candidates 0 and 2 so the project does not silently map everyday usage to one class.

The interface contract explicitly illustrates poodle returning candidates 6, 7, 8. FCI 172 covers these three sizes within one standard. The two chosen morphology traits are shared and should not be used to distinguish Poodle sizes.

FCI 182 uses the name Schnauzer, while FCI 183 and FCI 181 use qualifying names. The project shares the broad term schnauzer across 9, 10, 11 in keeping with ambiguity handling. The selected coat and ear claims are shared.

FCI standard titles support Great Swiss Mountain Dog, Appenzeller Sennenhund / Appenzell Cattle Dog, Entlebuch Cattle Dog, Zwergschnauzer, Riesenschnauzer, Irish Red Setter, English Springer Spaniel, English Cocker Spaniel, Japanese Chin, Pekingese and Shih Tzu as source names behind the exact local labels. AKC directly documents Japanese Spaniel as the earlier name of Japanese Chin.

Local searchable translations, informal names and descriptive spellings were checked for class collision and intent. A lexical or official citation for every alias was outside the 29-source morphology review.
Suggested direct regression cases are husky, poodle, schnauzer, Siberian Husky, Toy Poodle, Standard Schnauzer and Border Collie. This review did not run the retrieval runtime.
